$comment: EnergyX Trust Layer — fact registry v2.
PROVENANCE, read this before demoing anything:
- The 'lh-*' facts were measured by Raj from Lighthouse 13.5.0 reports he ran
on 2026-10-08. He has the report URLs. These are solid.
- The 'ex-*' facts were read off energyx.com on 2026-10-08 via an automated
page fetch. They are marked verified:true so the assistant can use them,
BUT a transcription error is possible.
>>> Raj: before the demo, open energyx.com and eyeball these six by hand:
ex-patents, ex-funding, ex-dle-time, ex-water-reduction,
ex-bg-capacity, ex-gm. Ten minutes. If one of them is wrong in front
of Teague, the whole registry loses its credibility.
- ex-ceo and ex-cmo are verified:false. Raj checks https://energyx.com/about-us/
by hand, then flips them. Until then the assistant cannot see them.
approvedAt is null on every EnergyX fact, always. Raj is not EnergyX.
basisSource: 'stated' means the cited source itself says what the figure
counts. 'inferred' means it does not, and the basis here is this registry's
reading. The gap between those two is the entire point of the project.
Byte facts (unit 'KiB'): numeric is KiB exactly as Lighthouse reports it;
value is decimal MB = KiB * 1024 / 1e6, one decimal place.
tests/unit/byte-facts.test.ts recomputes every one.

facts.label: DLE processing time
facts.basis: Figure given in the homepage comparison table, contrasted against 12 to 18 months for conventional evaporation. The table does not define what counts as the start or end of the process.

source.title: EnergyX homepage, conventional vs DLE comparison

alsoPublishedAs.basis: Stated in the FAQ section of the same homepage: direct lithium extraction reduces the conventional timeline to hours.

facts.note: Both figures appear on the SAME page. This is the clearest example in the registry: one subject, two published answers, neither stating what it measures. Present it as a metadata gap, never as an error.

facts.label: Freshwater reduction vs conventional extraction
facts.basis: Described in the homepage FAQ as the reduction achieved versus conventional extraction. The FAQ also gives the underlying figures: up to 400,000 gallons per ton conventional, around 800 gallons per ton with DLE.
facts.note: The two figures EnergyX publishes imply roughly a 99.8% reduction, not 'over 90%'. Technically 99.8% IS over 90%, so the claim is not wrong — it is conservative to the point of hiding its own strength. This is the one finding in the registry where the correction makes EnergyX's claim stronger. Lead with it when talking to the CMO.

facts.label: Freshwater use, conventional extraction
facts.basis: Stated in the homepage FAQ as the freshwater consumption of conventional extraction per ton of lithium.

facts.label: Freshwater use, EnergyX DLE
facts.basis: Stated in the homepage FAQ as EnergyX's freshwater consumption per ton of lithium.

facts.label: Freshwater reduction implied by EnergyX's own figures
facts.basis: Arithmetic by this registry from two figures in the homepage FAQ: around 800 gallons per ton with DLE against up to 400,000 gallons per ton conventional. EnergyX does not publish this percentage; the same FAQ states the reduction as over 90%.
facts.note: tests/unit/byte-facts.test.ts recomputes this from ex-water-conventional and ex-water-dle.

facts.label: Patents
facts.basis: Figure in the homepage company-stats band. The homepage does not state whether this counts granted patents only, or granted plus pending applications, or which technology areas are included.

alsoPublishedAs.basis: TODO(content) — Raj to confirm exact wording. If the blog says 'patents and applications', set basisSource to stated.

facts.note: If the blog and the SEC filings do state what they count and the homepage does not, the finding is that the most-read page is the only one without a basis. Verify before claiming that.

facts.label: Founded
facts.basis: Year given in the homepage company-stats band. Corresponds to the founding of Energy Exploration Technologies, Inc.

facts.label: Team
facts.basis: Labelled 'Members' in the homepage company-stats band. The page does not state whether this counts employees only, or includes contractors and advisors.

facts.label: Funding raised
facts.basis: Figure in the homepage company-stats band. The page does not state whether this is cumulative capital raised across all rounds, includes grants and strategic investment, or is equity only.

facts.label: Acres
facts.basis: Figure in the homepage company-stats band. The page does not say where these acres are, whether they are owned, leased or under option, or whether the figure is gross or net.

facts.label: Projects
facts.basis: Count in the homepage company-stats band, matching the five projects shown on the page: Black Giant, Lonestar, Powder Hound, Battery Mecca and Split. These are at different stages, from pilot to planned commercial facility.

facts.label: General Motors investment
facts.basis: Stated in the homepage FAQ as part of GM's battery supply chain strategy. The FAQ does not give an amount, a date or a stake size.

facts.label: EnergyX chief executive (CEO)
facts.basis: Named in the Leadership section of EnergyX's About page, under the title "Founder & CEO". Read off the page by an automated fetch on 2026-11-08 and not yet checked by hand, so this fact stays unverified until it is.

facts.label: EnergyX chief marketing officer (CMO)
facts.basis: Named in the Leadership section of EnergyX's About page, under the title "Chief Marketing Officer". Read off the page by an automated fetch on 2026-11-08 and not yet checked by hand, so this fact stays unverified until it is.

facts.label: Black Giant location
facts.value: Salar de Punta Negra, Antofagasta, Chile
facts.basis: Location as given on the homepage project card for Black Giant.

facts.label: Black Giant resource area
facts.basis: Described on the homepage project card as a lithium resource of this area. The card does not state the tenure type.

facts.label: Black Giant capacity
facts.basis: Given on the homepage project card as Phase I and II combined. This is a planned capacity, not current production.
facts.note: The Black Giant project page renders this as 52,500 (captured in the Lighthouse layout-shift audit) while the homepage rounds it to 53K. Same figure, two presentations — a rounding-consistency case, much milder than the days/hours one.

facts.label: Black Giant in-situ resource
facts.basis: Given on the homepage project card as an in-situ figure. An in-situ resource is lithium estimated to be present in the ground, not lithium that is recoverable or economic to produce.

facts.label: Lonestar DOE grant
facts.basis: Described on the homepage project card as a U.S. Department of Energy grant backing the Lonestar project in the Smackover region, Texarkana, Texas.

facts.label: Lonestar target capacity
facts.basis: Given on the homepage project card as a target for 2030. Lithium hydroxide, not lithium carbonate equivalent — a different product from the Black Giant figure.

facts.label: Powder Hound capacity
facts.basis: Given on the homepage project card as projected capacity for a commercial DLE facility at the Great Salt Lake, Ogden, Utah, with Compass Minerals.
facts.note: Use the precise noun for the Compass Minerals relationship. The homepage says 'with Compass Minerals'; earlier reporting described a non-binding MOU. Do not upgrade it to a partnership without a source that says so.

facts.label: Battery Mecca target capacity
facts.basis: Given on the homepage project card as a target for the Smackover region, Texas.

facts.label: Black Giant page total payload
facts.basis: Total network payload for energyx.com/black-giant/ measured by Lighthouse 13.5.0 on an emulated Moto G Power with Slow 4G throttling, single page session, initial load.

facts.label: Black Giant hero video size
facts.basis: Single file PBG60secVideo1.mp4 from media.energyx.com, autoplay loop playsinline with preload=metadata. Lighthouse identifies this element as the Largest Contentful Paint.

source.title: Lighthouse report, /black-giant/, payload and LCP audits

facts.label: Black Giant second video size
facts.basis: Single file Energy-X-Final_V1.mp4, the second video file on energyx.com/black-giant/, listed in the Lighthouse network payload audit for the same page load as the hero video.

facts.label: Black Giant video bytes, both files
facts.basis: Sum of the two video files on the page, PBG60secVideo1.mp4 and Energy-X-Final_V1.mp4, from the same Lighthouse run. Lighthouse lists each file; the sum is arithmetic by this registry.

facts.label: Black Giant page bytes other than video
facts.basis: Total page payload minus the two video files, all from the same Lighthouse run: everything the page transfers that is not one of those two videos. Arithmetic by this registry.

facts.basis: Total transferred for this demo's deployed /black-giant/ across 12 requests, measured by Lighthouse 13.5.0, mobile, US West (us-west1) test location, initial load. lighthouse-metrics reported 930 kB (decimal kilobytes, 930,000 bytes); stored as 908.2 KiB under the registry's byte convention.

facts.label: Homepage bytes served from Box
facts.basis: Third-party transfer from boxcloud.com, which Lighthouse's video-captions audit shows is the delivery host for the homepage hero video element, whose source is an energyx.box.com shared link. 84% of the page's total payload; the percentage is arithmetic from the two measured figures.

source.title: Lighthouse report, homepage, third-party, payload and captions audits

facts.note: Frame as a delivery-pipeline gap. Never as a criticism of the video itself or of who produced it.

facts.label: Homepage second video size
facts.basis: Single file EnergyX-2.mp4 from media.energyx.com, listed in the Lighthouse network payload audit for the homepage, separate from the hero video served from Box.

facts.label: Homepage bytes other than video
facts.basis: Total homepage payload minus the bytes served from Box (the hero video) and the second video file EnergyX-2.mp4, all from the same Lighthouse run. Arithmetic by this registry.

facts.label: Homepage LCP element
facts.basis: Lighthouse identifies the paragraph beginning 'We use analytics and marketing cookies' as the Largest Contentful Paint element at 5.9s, with 180ms time to first byte and 2,170ms element render delay.
facts.note: The server is fast — 180ms TTFB. The delay is entirely client side. The largest thing painted is the consent banner, meaning nothing meaningful has rendered.

facts.label: Homepage Cumulative Layout Shift
facts.basis: Lighthouse 13.5.0 lab measurement, emulated Moto G Power, Slow 4G. A lab figure, not field data from real users.

facts.label: Homepage Total Blocking Time
facts.basis: Lighthouse 13.5.0 lab measurement, emulated Moto G Power, Slow 4G: time during page load when the main thread was blocked long enough to delay a tap. A lab figure, not field data from real users.

facts.label: Agentic Browsing score, Black Giant
facts.basis: Lighthouse 13.5.0 Agentic Browsing category, which checks whether a page is navigable by AI agents and whether WebMCP integrations are valid. llms.txt, ai-catalog.json and registered WebMCP tools are all reported not applicable, meaning absent.

facts.label: Share of first-load JavaScript that is React DOM and the Next app-router client (local)
facts.basis: The two largest shared scripts, identified by the library code they contain (React DOM's Fiber and hydrateRoot code; the app router's prefetch and navigation code), total 119,777 compressed bytes of the 145,660 that every route except the Black Giant page loads. Measured on 2026-11-03 against a local `next start`, 390px viewport, by listing each script request with Playwright. Attribution is by library fingerprint, not module-level attribution, so the boundary of each library is not module-exact. Rounded to a whole percent.

facts.label: Share of first-load JavaScript in the one script that is this site's own code (local)
facts.basis: The AskForm script, the only script that is this repo's own code rather than shared with a framework component, is 2,659 compressed bytes of the 145,660 that every route except the Black Giant page loads. Measured on 2026-11-03 against a local `next start`, 390px viewport. The mobile menu shares a script with next/link and the hero video with next/image; those were not separated, so this is a floor for this site's code, not a total. Attribution is by library fingerprint, not module-level attribution, so it is not module-exact. Rounded to a whole percent.
